name: Gauge-Detection
description: Gauge-Detection is an image-text benchmark for detecting and localizing the key components of gauges in photographs. Each sample pairs a gauge image with a prompt and requires bounding boxes for the gauge base, tip, minimum, and maximum regions.
card_text: Gauge-Detection contains 200 image-text samples focused on visual object detection of analog gauge parts. Each item provides an image file path and a generic text prompt that asks a model to identify gauge components. The expected output is a set of bounding boxes for four gauge parts—base, tip, minimum, and maximum—each represented as a four-number coordinate box. The dataset is designed to evaluate object detection and spatial localization capabilities in real-world instrument imagery. Images are natural photographs of gauges with varying viewpoints and scales, and prompts are placeholders for model-specific instructions. Annotations are structured as a list of part-name-to-bbox mappings.

context.semantics: The image file path points to a photograph of a gauge or metering instrument. It is the main visual context from which the model must detect and localize gauge components.

question.semantics: A short placeholder prompt instructing the model to perform gauge-part detection. It serves as the task instruction paired with the image.

bbox.semantics: A list of bounding-box annotations for four gauge parts: base, tip, minimum, and maximum. Each entry maps a part name to a four-number box (e.g., x, y, width, height) locating that part in the image.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample contains an image file path representing a gauge photograph, a short generic prompt instructing detection, and an output list of bounding boxes. The bbox output has four named entries—base, tip, minimum, and maximum—each with a four-number coordinate box that localizes the corresponding gauge component in the image.
